It is a full page of mercantesca on the recto and about 16 lines on the verso; the recto opens 'Spectabilis vir ...' in clear and the verso address reads 'Spectabili viro Fra[n]cesco ... oratori ... ' (rest not legible), so the hand is ordinary clear cursive; the odd groups (e.g. 'zyzz7te' on recto line 9) cannot be separated from abbreviations without a full palaeographic reading, and no run of symbol cipher or gloss is visible. The foot of the verso reads '... a dì 17 d(i) l[u]glio 1459' (the second digit is a looped merchant 4, the third a 5), not 1499: Piero di Lorenzo (born 1472) cannot be the sender, so the inventory's attribution is wrong (Piero di Cosimo, 1459, is the candidate). Lorenzo's Lettere do not reach 1459 and were not searched. Needs a full reading of the clear text to locate any cipher words before a verdict.

title: Roberto Acciaiuoli, Florentine orator in France, Amiens 23 October 1513: two sides of homophonic cipher, bare; a glossed letter of the same day gives the key
correspondents: Roberto Acciaiuoli, orator at the French court -> [Giuliano de' Medici / the Medici in Florence]
language: Italian (sign cipher with superscript homophone marks)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 192 (old c. 234)
folio_note: One leaf: recto opens "Mag.ce Vir" then about 15 lines of letter-signs, many with small superscript digits (3, 4, 5); the verso about 14 more lines of the same. MAP inventory vol. 3: "Robertus Acciarolus, orator. Ex Amiens, 1513 ott. 23, n. 192" (no cipher flag).
status: Bare (900 px, recto and verso). Key material: doc. 190 (c. 232), Acciaiuoli's cipher letter of the same day in the same system (signed "Robertus Acciarolus", "Ex Amiens die xxiii Octobris MDXIII"), and doc. 191 (c. 233), "Copia di lettera di Ruberto Acciaioli da Amiens ...", which repeats the text of 190 in clear ("Oltre alle lettere publiche ... Sanseverino ... arrivò adì xx la sera"): a full plaintext for 190.
why: The Florentine ambassador at Louis XII's court in the year after the Medici restoration; the key can be rebuilt from 190/191 and 192 read.
verify: Align 190 with 191 to rebuild the homophonic table (superscripts included); apply to 192 r-v.

vetting_note: probable plaintext not checked: LXXII 192 is not a second private letter but a cipher copy of Acciaiuoli's public despatch of 23 Oct 1513. Its recto is headed in a contemporary hand 'Copia della l[ette]ra c[...]' and opens 'Mag(nifi)ci D(omi)ni etc.', the verso closes 'raccomandarmi alle Sig. V(ost)re ... Ex Amiens die xxiii Octobris MDXIII, Robertus Acciarolus', while 190 (to a single 'Mag.ce Vir', signed the same day) says in clear 'Ultra le lettere publ(iche) delle qual sara con questa el doppio'. Acciaiuoli's letter of 23 Oct 1513 to the Dieci di Balia survives at ASF, Dieci di Balia, Responsive 118, c. 139r (cited with the 20 Oct letter at c. 138r in Annuarium Historiae Conciliorum 1984, Google Books mADZAAAAMAAJ, feed snippet). If that original is in clear or carries its decipherment, 192's text is on record. Needs the Dieci Responsive 118 c. 139 (not online) or the 1984 article's text. Everything else checked: see notes.
